metadata.methods_description: EEG recordings were collected from 8 channels (Fz, Cz, P3, Pz, P4, PO7, PO8, Oz) according to the 10-20 electrode placement standard, grounded to AFz and referenced to right mastoid (M2). Sampling frequency was 256 Hz. Participants performed 3 sessions with 7 recordings each, varying stimulus count (4-9) and flash type (standard flash or superimposed cartoon face). Event markers encoded experimental phases (Fixation, Target Presentation, Preparation, Stimulation, Rest) and stimulus identity.

citation_details.title: The quantifying of consciousness
citation_details.author: Jonathan Jared Wilson
citation_details.abstract: The Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR) theory proposes that consciousness arises from quantum processes in microtubules within neurons. However, the theory has faced challenges due to the lack of empirical evidence supporting its claims. In this study, we present a novel approach to validate the Orch-OR theory by integrating total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy and kymograph analysis data with relevant datasets from the OpenNeuro platform. Our results provide strong empirical support for the key predictions of the Orch-OR theory, demonstrating the presence of quantum processes in microtubules and their correlation with conscious states. This interdisciplinary approach bridges the gap between theoretical quantum neuroscience and empirical observations, paving the way for a more comprehensive understanding of the nature of consciousness.

citation_details.title: Single-Option P300-BCI Performance Is Affected by Visual Stimulation Conditions
citation_details.author: Juan David Chailloux Peguero, Omar Mendoza-Montoya, Javier M. Antelis
citation_details.abstract: The P300 paradigm is one of the most promising techniques for its robustness and reliability in Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) applications, but it is not exempt from shortcomings. The present work studied single-trial classification effectiveness in distinguishing between target and non-target responses considering two conditions of visual stimulation and the variation of the number of symbols presented to the user in a single-option visual frame. In addition, we also investigated the relationship between the classification results of target and non-target events when training and testing the machine-learning model with datasets containing different stimulation conditions and different number of symbols. To this end, we designed a P300 experimental protocol considering, as conditions of stimulation: the color highlighting or the superimposing of a cartoon face and from four to nine options. These experiments were carried out with 19 healthy subjects in 3 sessions. The results showed that the Event-Related Potentials (ERP) responses and the classification accuracy are stronger with cartoon faces as stimulus type and similar irrespective of the amount of options. In addition, the classification performance is reduced when using datasets with different type of stimulus, but it is similar when using datasets with different the number of symbols. These results have a special connotation for the design of systems, in which it is intended to elicit higher levels of evoked potentials and, at the same time, optimize training time.

citation_details.title: P300 BCI EEG dataset (Chailloux Peguero et al. 2020)
citation_details.author: J. David Chailloux Peguero, Omar Mendoza-Montoya, Javier M. Antelis
citation_details.abstract: A P300 brain-computer interface EEG dataset comprising recordings from 19 healthy participants across 3 sessions. The study investigates the effects of visual stimulation conditions (standard flash versus cartoon face stimuli) on P300-BCI performance using an 8-channel montage sampled at 256 Hz, with data collected using a P300 paradigm across 5 grid sizes and including target and non-target event classifications. This is a BIDS-formatted derivative dataset converted from OpenNeuro ds003190 using the MOABB pipeline.
